items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Terminology 83:1
items.html: (To the question) What are sources and streams? The Yesod of the male is called a source, which is the source of the influx, and the aspect of the direct light. And the Yesod of the upper Nukva is called a stream, in the verse "he will drink from the stream by the way, therefore he will raise his head," and as the Rav explained, that all the Mochin of ZA come from the power that he receives from the Yesod of Ima, called the stream. Therefore the illuminations drawn from the Yesod of Aba to ZA are called sources, and the illuminations drawn from the Yesod of Ima are called streams. (Item 62).
